data.name: Divide
data.detailed_description:
Divide is a character-driven, science fiction action/adventure game with a modern take on isometric adventures of the past. Search for clues that reveal new insight into the story, interact with fully realized characters, and combat enemies by hacking out of sight, or launching a direct assault.

Combat in Divide is stacked heavily against the player. Each encounter has the potential to get completely out of hand. Combat areas, big and small, can be directly assaulted using a futuristic side-arm and the potential aid of an ally. The player also has the option to slink through using stealth and misdirection by hacking the enemy’s own communication.

The player moves with the left stick and aims with the right stick. Everything else from sprinting to shooting a sidearm to interacting with the main character’s augmented reality interface are mapped to the buttons on the top of the controller. Fingers and thumbs stay put, while the player stays in control.

Power up derelict complexes, unlock jammed doors, and delve into long abandoned computer networks as you dust off the secrets of the mighty Vestige Corporation. Players explore expansive isometric environments and stroll through deep matte paintings that bring Divide’s world to life.

*Divide requires an XInput compatible gamepad. XBox 360, XBox One, PS4, Steam Controller or similar.

Divide is a character-driven, science fiction action/adventure game with a modern take on isometric adventures of the past. In this game you have to search for clues that reveal new insights into the story, interact with fully realized characters, and combat enemies by hacking out of sight, or launching a direct assault.

[h3] ⚔ Gameplay: [/h3] 
Rate: ★★☆☆☆ 
 
At its core is a point and click action-adventure game. The gameplay revolving this game is rather simple: Interact with objects, hack or extract intel by simply clicking and in some cases defend yourself by aiming and shooting at enemies like robot sentinels or guards. It involves a lot of backtracking and figuring out how to solve areas without much indication or hinting

Aside from hacking, you also have simple combat where you use a special taser gun to take down robots or guards.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2891111440

[h3] 😄 Fun: [/h3] 
Rate: ★★☆☆☆ 
 
Despite the interesting story and the captivating characters, the gameplay has left me wanting some more. Aiming and shooting is very difficult and often times I’d end up dying because I can’t aim fast enough. Having to run out of combat when things get difficult is rather unpleasant.

Second issue with this game in regards to my fun with it is the fact that the game has had 2 times save file corrupted issues with me. I don’t know what was causing it, but I’ve noticed it happening while trying to switch between PC and Steam Deck. I’m not 100% sure that’s the case, but be aware about that. If you want to finish this game as I did, you have to consider having a full playthrough otherwise you’ll end up like me wasting several hours of gameplay and having to repeat the game again from scratch. That’s not a fun experience.
 
[h3] 🏞 Visuals: [/h3] 
Rate: ★★★☆☆ 
 
Visually this game looks pretty nice in the gameplay area. I really like how it looks, but fails to impress me when it comes to areas where you switch from Isometric to a 2D style or something of a sort. I feel that it fails to have a consistency in that area.

Second, the characters have no animation and that’s fine, but often times they pose in ridiculous poses that it’s difficult not to laugh when you see the faces they pull off.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2891109999

[h3] 🔊 Sound: [/h3] 
Rate: ★★★★★ 
 
I think the game does an excellent job with music and sound effect. It feels really polished in this area and voice actors performed really well, portraying the characters well and telling the story well enough to keep me interested.
 
[h3] 📖 Story: [/h3] 
Rate: ★★★★★ 
 
Divide dives into an interesting sci-fi story where you play as David, a father in his late 30s, maybe early 40s who’s looking after his daughter while his wife mysteriously died in a laboratory experiment.

The game start where you receive a strange case from your friend, that contains special lenses that allows you to see and interact with the world as well an strange orb that activates and teleports you into a strange futuristic place that have to figure out what is going on and how you can return back home.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2888728283
 
[h3] 🧵 Length: [/h3] 
 
☑️  Short 
☑️ Average 
🔲 Long  
🔲 Unlimited 
 
This game takes between 6 hours to 12 to complete if you want to achieve full completion.
 
[h3] 🧩 Difficulty: [/h3] 
 
🔲 Easy 
☑️ Normal 
🔲 Hard 
🔲 Brutally Hard 
🔲 Impossible 
 
I’ve not had much struggle with this game over the fact that aiming with a controller takes time getting used to and even then it can be rather clunky. Enemy AI is rather dumb in some cases intentionally so you can avoid conflict and just run through enemy sometimes freely without taking damage. If you do happen to take damage, your health recovers quickly to 100% once you’re out of combat, so you can go again in the enemy sight and try to eliminate them.

It can get a bit difficult when there’s waves of soldiers coming at your way, but if you position yourself right you should be alright.

[h3] ⭕Conclusion: [/h3] 
Divide is an interesting console port, with an amazing soundtrack and captivating story, but horribly fails in the technical area and repetitive and boring gameplay. Backtracking isn’t done very well to keep the whole gameplay exciting and often times repetition can kill quickly your joy to want to finish it. Never the less, the story might be the only thing that will keep you until the end.
